We raised a $13.5M Series A from Standard Capital, Y Combinator, Moonfire, Burst Capital, IrregEx, and the Agent Fund. We are a small team in San Francisco, and we work in person.

About the role

Weave's pipeline has been built by founders and a small GTM team. It works. Now we need someone to turn that into a repeatable outbound engine.

You will be our first BDR. You will start conversations with CTOs and VPs of Engineering who are under pressure to prove that AI coding tools are paying off, and who cannot answer that question with the dashboards they have today. Your job is to find those leaders, make the problem urgent, earn the right to a real conversation, and create qualified pipeline.

This is not a role where you inherit a finished script and run sequences all day. You will sit next to our founders and GTM team, learn how engineering leaders think, test messaging in the market, and write the outbound playbook that the next five BDRs will use.

You will report to Adam (CEO, previously scaled sales teams to $30M ARR) and work daily with our Founding GTM Engineer and marketing lead.

What you will actually do

  • Create qualified pipeline. Research target accounts, identify the right engineering leaders, and turn cold accounts into booked meetings for our AEs and founders.

  • Write outbound that sounds human. Build sharp, account-specific messaging across email, phone, LinkedIn, and other channels. No generic sequences.

  • Work events and dinners. Join us at engineering leadership events, start conversations in the room, and follow up fast enough to turn interest into pipeline.

  • Build the playbook. Test personas, segments, hooks, objections, and channels. Document what works so we can repeat it.

  • Close the feedback loop. Bring what prospects say back to founders, marketing, and product every week.

What we are looking for

Must-haves

  • Comfort on the phone. You can open a cold call, ask a useful question, listen, and earn a next step.

  • Strong writing and research skills. You can find a real reason to contact an account and explain it in two sentences.

  • Curiosity about how software gets built. You want to learn how engineering teams work, how AI coding tools are changing that, and how technical leaders evaluate new software.

  • Good judgment about quality. You would rather book the right meeting than hit a vanity activity number.

  • Resilience and follow-through. You handle rejection, keep your standards high, and stay organized across a large account set.

  • Startup readiness. You are comfortable testing ideas, working without a finished playbook, and making your own progress visible.

  • Able to work in person from our San Francisco office five days a week.

Nice-to-haves

  • One year of outbound SDR or BDR experience in B2B software, with evidence that you consistently book qualified meetings.

  • Experience prospecting into developer tools, infrastructure, engineering analytics, or another technical category.

  • Familiarity with CTOs, VPs of Engineering, or engineering managers as buyers.

  • Experience at an early-stage startup or helping stand up a new outbound motion.

  • Hands-on experience with Clay, HubSpot, lemlist, or similar tools.

  • A real interest in AI coding tools and how they are changing software teams.

What this role is not

  • Not remote. You will build the motion alongside the team in San Francisco.

  • Not an activity contest. A dashboard full of calls matters less than whether anyone should take the meeting.

  • Not a mature sales org. There is no finished script, perfect data, or documented objection library. You will help build those.

  • Not selling a checkbox. You will need to explain why engineering leaders need a new way to understand their teams.

What we offer

  • Compensation. $80,000 plus target variable $40,000 for OTE $120,000, plus meaningful early equity.

  • Benefits. Full health coverage, meals in the office, yearly team offsite, and a $500 learning stipend.

  • Real ownership. Build the outbound motion instead of inheriting someone else's playbook.

  • Direct access. Work daily with founders who have done this before and can act on your feedback quickly.

  • A product with proof. Over 300 customers, including Robinhood, Rho, PostHog, and Browserbase, and double-digit monthly growth since May 2025.

  • A clear path. Strong performance here leads to AE, GTM leadership, or building out the BDR team you helped design.

Interview process

  1. Intro call (15 minutes). Your background, your outbound experience, and what interests you about Weave.

  2. Mock cold call (30 minutes). You call a VP of Engineering at a target account. One of us plays the prospect. We want to see how you open, ask questions, handle pushback, and earn a next step.

  3. CEO interview (30 minutes). How you learn a market and how you think about pipeline quality.

  4. Team lunch. Meet the people you would work with every day and see if we are a mutual fit.

Our mission

Software is being built differently now. Engineering leaders are managing humans and AI agents together, and the tools they use to understand their teams were built for a world that no longer exists. Weave gives them the truth about how work gets done, so they can make better decisions faster.

Weave (YC W25) is building the definitive platform for understanding and improving how engineering teams work. We believe the way engineering output is measured today is fundamentally broken and that modern AI can give teams a far more accurate and actionable view of productivity, impact and collaboration.

Trusted by 200+ customers such as Robinhood, Rho, PostHog and Browserbase, we’ve delivered consistent double-digit month-over-month revenue growth since May and are looking to accelerate our growth.

As Weave’s Founding AI Engineer, your job is to build AI to understand and improve the work that software engineers do. You’ll be building our processes and standards as you go to make building every incremental feature easier. Your goal will be to delight customers with intelligence that makes their job 10x easier.

We’ve raised a $4.2M seed round and are backed by Moonfire, Burst capital and Y Combinator (W25).

This is a rare opportunity to join at the ground floor and shape how millions of engineers and leaders understand engineering work.

What We’re Building

Weave is rethinking engineering output from first principles.

We use AI to:

  • Understand how engineers actually work (not just what they ship)

  • Surface meaningful insights about productivity, quality, collaboration and impact

  • Help teams improve outcomes without vanity metrics or surveillance

Our goal is not to optimize for “more output,” but for better engineering.

The Team You’ll Work With

You’ll work directly with:

  • Andrew (CTO) – previously a founding engineer at Causal, MIT alum. Andrew has been in your shoes and is deeply committed to providing the mentorship, ownership and growth he had as an early engineer.

  • Adam (CEO) – leads sales and customer discovery. Adam is a former sales executive at multiple high-growth startups and deeply embedded with customers and scaled multiple sales teams from $0-30M in ARR.

This is a small, intense, highly collaborative team. You will have real ownership from day one.

Must haves

You are a good fit for Weave if you are a formidable engineer. This means you stop at nothing to accomplish your goal. We don't care much about your current skills or even what you've done before; we care that you will be able to do anything you set your mind to.

You must also be pragmatic. Weave is a startup so something is always on fire. You need to know when to let little fires burn and when to break out the extinguisher.

You must be a very good engineer who's committed to becoming a great engineer. The slope is more important than the Y-intercept.

You must be empathetic. We're building products for other people, so you need to be able to understand how other people think and why.

You must care about helping other software engineering teams be great. If that's not an exciting mission for you, it will be hard to stay motivated through the inevitable highs and lows.

You must be an excellent communicator. You’ll be working on a product that’s communicating with millions of engineers and leaders, so you need to be clear.

Finally you must be gritty. You should be accustomed to picking the hard option and pushing through it.

This role is 5 days in office in SF

Nice to haves

(Please feel free to apply even if some or all of these don't apply to you!)

Our tech stack is React + TypeScript on the frontend, Go on the backend, and Python for ML. Experience with any of those three languages is a bonus.

If you've already done lots of thinking about engineering productivity and how to improve it, that's great and we want to hear about it!

We hope your design sensibilities are passable.

Why Join

  • Competitive pay + early equity

  • Health/vision/dental insurance covered

  • Free lunch/dinners/snacks

  • Yearly team offsite with regular team events

  • Yearly $500 learning/development stipend

  • Get to work in SF with one of the fastest moving teams (95%+ percentile code output)

About the interview

  1. 15-minute intro call

  2. Take home assessment

  3. One-hour technical interview with our CTO, Andrew

  4. One-hour technical interview with our CTO, Andrew

  5. 3-5 day paid work trial

You'll own the open-source Weave Router, the content and demos that teach engineers how to measure AI-era engineering, and the community of developers who make Weave the default in their orgs.

  • Surface meaningful insights about productivity, quality, collaboration and impact

  • Help teams improve outcomes without vanity metrics or surveillance

  • Andrew (CTO) – previously a founding engineer at Causal, MIT alum. Andrew has been in your shoes and is deeply committed to providing the mentorship, ownership and growth he had as an early engineer.

  • Adam (CEO) – leads sales and customer discovery. Adam is a former sales executive at multiple high-growth startups and deeply embedded with customers and scaled multiple sales teams from $0-30M in ARR.

This is a small, intense, highly collaborative team. You will have real ownership from day one.

The Role

This isn't a traditional developer relations role. The closest thing we can describe it as is a mashup of software engineer, technical writer, video producer, and open-source maintainer.

You own the conversation with the engineers: the tech leads, staff engineers and engineering managers who install Weave and decide whether Weave is a tool they trust or a dashboard their boss bought. Engineers everywhere are asking the same question: "am I actually better with AI, and how would I know?" The person who answers it credibly, with working code and real data, in public, will earn the trust of every engineer we want as a customer. We want that person to be you.

Responsibilities

  • Build in public. Ship demos, integrations, plugins and sample projects on top of Weave and the Weave Router. Real code engineers can clone, not slideware.

  • Own the Weave Router community. Issues, PRs, releases, docs, contributors. Make the router the default way teams route prompts across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and whatever ships next.

  • Write the technical content. Deep dives, tutorials, benchmarks and integration guides that engineers cite. "We analyzed 2M PRs and here's what AI actually changed" is your kind of headline.

  • Own developer experience. Every integration should take minutes. You'll find the rough edges in our docs, SDKs and installers before customers do and fix them, in the docs or in the code.

  • Show up where engineers are. Meetups, hackathons, livestreams, podcasts, X, Hacker News. The Field CTO owns the keynote stage; you own the hallway track, the demo booth and the comments section.

  • Feed the community back into product. You'll hear what hundreds of engineers actually struggle with. Bring it home and sharpen our roadmap with it.

  • Partner with marketing and sales. Technical firepower for launches alongside our Founding Marketer. Technical credibility in deals alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers.

  • You're an engineer first. You've shipped production code and you still write it every week. You can build the demo, not just present it.

  • You write exceptionally well. Your posts, docs or READMEs have an audience because engineers found them useful, not because the SEO is good.

  • You've built an audience or a community. On X, YouTube, a newsletter, a Discord, or an open-source project people depend on. Not "a post did well once." You can show us the receipts.

  • You live the AI coding shift. You use Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar daily. Your opinions about models, tokens and agents come from your own terminal, not from a thread you read.

  • You care about how engineering is measured. You have real opinions on DORA, SPACE and DevEx, and on what changes when half the code is written by agents.

  • This role is 5 days in office in SF, with regular travel to meetups, hackathons and conferences

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior developer advocate, DevRel or developer education role at a developer tools, AI/ML or infrastructure company

  • You've maintained an open-source project, or been a core contributor to one that other people depend on

  • You've shipped something on top of LLM APIs, MCP servers or agent frameworks that real people used

  • You've produced demo videos, livestreams or a YouTube channel that grew on the strength of the work

  • Our tech stack is React + TypeScript on the frontend, Go on the backend, and Python for ML. The Weave Router is written in Go. Experience with any of those is a bonus.

  • Experience at an early-stage startup (Seed to Series B), even if it wasn't a DevRel role

Why Join

  • Competitive pay + early equity

  • Health/vision/dental insurance covered

  • Free lunch/dinners/snacks

  • Yearly team offsite with regular team events

  • Yearly $500 learning/development stipend

  • Get to work in SF with one of the fastest moving teams (99%+ percentile code output)

About the Interview

  1. 15-minute intro call

  2. 30-minute interview with our CEO, Adam

  3. 45-minute technical interview with our CTO, Andrew

  4. Give us a talk: a 15-minute technical talk or live demo, delivered as you would at a meetup

  5. 3-5 day paid work trial

Weave (YC W25) is building the definitive platform for understanding and improving how engineering teams work. We believe the way engineering output is measured today is fundamentally broken and that modern AI can give teams a far more accurate and actionable view of productivity, impact and collaboration.

Trusted by 200+ customers such as Robinhood, Rho, PostHog and Browserbase, we’ve delivered consistent double-digit month-over-month revenue growth since May and are looking to accelerate our growth.

As Weave’s Founding ML Engineer, your job is to build ML systems to understand and improve the work that software engineers do. You’ll be building our processes and standards as you go to make building every incremental feature and subsequent model easier. Your goal will be to delight customers with intelligence that makes their job 10x easier.

We've raised a $13.5 million Series A and are backed by Standard Capital, YCombinator, Moonfire, Burst Capital, IrregEx and the Agent Fund.

This is a rare opportunity to join at the ground floor and shape how millions of engineers and leaders understand engineering work.

What We’re Building

Weave is rethinking engineering output from first principles.

We use AI to:

  • Understand how engineers actually work (not just what they ship)

  • Surface meaningful insights about productivity, quality, collaboration and impact

  • Help teams improve outcomes without vanity metrics or surveillance

Our goal is not to optimize for “more output,” but for better engineering.

The Team You’ll Work With

You’ll work directly with:

  • Andrew (CTO) – previously a founding engineer at Causal, MIT alum. Andrew has been in your shoes and is deeply committed to providing the mentorship, ownership and growth he had as an early engineer.

  • Adam (CEO) – leads sales and customer discovery. Adam is a former sales executive at multiple high-growth startups and deeply embedded with customers and scaled multiple sales teams from $0-30M in ARR.

This is a small, intense, highly collaborative team. You will have real ownership from day one.

Must haves

You are a good fit for Weave if you are a formidable engineer. This means you stop at nothing to accomplish your goal. We don't care much about your current skills or even what you've done before; we care that you will be able to do anything you set your mind to.

You must also be pragmatic. Weave is a startup so something is always on fire. You need to know when to let little fires burn and when to break out the extinguisher.

You must have experience with shipping ML systems to production, end to end. From selecting an appropriate data set, to feature engineering, to model design, to deployment & iteration.

You must be a very good engineer who's committed to becoming a great engineer. The slope is more important than the Y-intercept.

You must be empathetic. We're building products for other people, so you need to be able to understand how other people think and why.

You must care about helping other software engineering teams be great. If that's not an exciting mission for you, it will be hard to stay motivated through the inevitable highs and lows.

You must be an excellent communicator. You'll be working on a product that's communicating with millions of engineers and leaders, so you need to be clear.

Finally you must be gritty. You should be accustomed to picking the hard option and pushing through it.

This role is 5 days in office in SF

Nice to haves

(Please feel free to apply even if some or all of these don't apply to you!)

Our tech stack is React + TypeScript on the frontend, Go on the backend, and Python for ML. Experience with any of those three languages is a bonus.

If you've already done lots of thinking about engineering productivity and how to improve it, that's great and we want to hear about it!

Why Join

  • Competitive pay + early equity

  • Health/vision/dental insurance covered

  • Free lunch/dinners/snacks

  • Yearly team offsite with regular team events

  • Yearly $500 learning/development stipend

  • Get to work in SF with one of the fastest moving teams (95%+ percentile code output)

About the interview

  1. 15-minute intro call

  2. Take home assessment

  3. One-hour technical interview with our CTO, Andrew

  4. One-hour technical interview with our CTO, Andrew

As Weave's Founding Creative Marketer, your job is to make Weave feel inevitable. You will turn Weave into the brand the best engineering teams in the world default to.

What We’re Building

Weave is rethinking engineering output from first principles.

We use AI to:

  • Understand how engineers actually work (not just what they ship)

  • Surface meaningful insights about productivity, quality, collaboration and impact

  • Help teams improve outcomes without vanity metrics or surveillance

Our goal is not to optimize for “more output,” but for better engineering.

  • Andrew (CTO) – previously a founding engineer at Causal, MIT alum. Andrew has been in your shoes and is deeply committed to providing the mentorship, ownership and growth he had as an early engineer.

  • Adam (CEO) – leads sales and customer discovery. Adam is a former sales executive at multiple high-growth startups and deeply embedded with customers and scaled multiple sales teams from $0-30M in ARR.

This is a small, intense, highly collaborative team. You will have real ownership from day one.

The Role

This isn't a traditional marketing role and we're not looking for a traditional marketer. The closest thing we can describe it as is a mashup of product marketing manager, content engineer, creative director, and video producer.

You'll be responsible for shaping the product story, writing the words, running launches, designing the graphics, and shipping campaigns. We launch tier-1A products on a cadence most companies can't match, and we want every launch to feel inevitable by the time it ships: primed by content, sequenced across channels, and impossible to ignore.

This is a rare opportunity to take real ownership over launches that move the business. Not to assist on someone else's strategy, not to optimize a slice of a funnel, but to own the thing end to end and be measured on whether it drove pipeline, signups, and brand. If you've been waiting for the role where you actually get the keys, this is it.

Responsibilities

  • Own launches end to end. Plan, sequence and ship tier-1 product launches. From positioning and naming to the launch video, the LinkedIn thread, the landing page, the customer quotes, and the follow-on content that keeps it alive for two weeks instead of two days.

  • Build the creative. You're the one making the assets, not just briefing them. Launch videos, ads, landing pages, blog graphics, demo edits, social cuts. You can take an idea from concept to shipped asset without waiting on a freelancer.

  • Build the content engine. Write and edit posts, threads, blogs, case studies, and launch collateral that get shared bay people we want as customers. You'll be both the writer and the editor, pushing the bar on every piece that goes out.

  • Run the growth playbook. Design, run, and measure experiments across organic social, paid, SEO, lifecycle, partnerships, and community. Kill what doesn't work, double down on what does.

  • Partner with product. Sit in the room when we're scoping the next release. Push back on launches that won't land. Sharpen the ones that will.

  • Build the brand. Weave should feel like the obvious choice for the best engineering teams in the world. You're the person making sure every touchpoint reinforces that.

  • Be flexible. Some days you'll be writing copy, others you'll be in Premiere or Figma, briefing a podcast guest, or wiring up an attribution pipeline. We're inventing the function as we go.

Qualifications

Must-Have

  • Proven track record on launches. You've helped launch content that drove pipeline and you can show us the receipts.

  • You've gone viral on on X and LinkedIn, repeatedly. Not "a post did well once." You've repeatedly produced content that broke out and you can explain why it worked.

  • You write exceptionally well. Not just "good for a marketer." You can write a LinkedIn post that gets shared, a blog post that gets cited and a launch announcement that makes engineers stop scrolling.

  • You have product taste. You can tell the difference between a launch that's worth the effort and one that isn't, and you can articulate why.

  • You move fast and own outcomes. You don't wait for a brief. You write the brief, ship the thing, and report on what happened.

  • You care about developer tools. You don't have to be an engineer, but you have to genuinely care about the audience: what they read, what they share, what they roll their eyes at.

  • This role is 5 days in office in SF

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience at an early-stage startup (Seed to Series B), even if it wasn't a marketing role

  • Background marketing developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or infrastructure software

  • Editorial or journalism background. You've worked somewhere where the bar on writing was high.

  • You've shipped a product yourself, run a side project, or worked closely enough with engineers to think like one

  • You've run your own newsletter, YouTube channel, or creator account that grew on the strength of the work

Why Join

  • Competitive pay + early equity

  • Health/vision/dental insurance covered

  • Free lunch/dinners/snacks

  • Yearly team offsite with regular team events

  • Yearly $500 learning/development stipend

  • Get to work in SF with one of the fastest moving teams (95%+ percentile code output)

About the interview

  1. 15-minute intro call

  2. Take home assignment

  3. 30-minute interview with CEO

  4. 30-minute interview with Founding GTM Engineer

  5. 3-5 day paid work trial. You'll plan and execute a real launch with us.

Weave (YC W25) is building the definitive platform for understanding and improving how engineering teams work. We believe the way engineering output is measured today is fundamentally broken and that modern AI can give teams a far more accurate and actionable view of productivity, impact and collaboration.

Trusted by 200+ customers such as Robinhood, Rho, PostHog and Browserbase, we’ve delivered consistent double-digit month-over-month revenue growth since May and are looking to accelerate our growth.

We want to hire an exceptional forward deployed engineer to help us make sure everyone gets the most out of our product.

We've raised a $13.5 million Series A and are backed by Standard Capital, YCombinator, Moonfire, Burst Capital, IrregEx and the Agent Fund.

This is a rare opportunity to join at the ground floor and shape how millions of engineers and leaders understand engineering work.

What We’re Building

Weave is rethinking engineering output from first principles.

We use AI to:

  • Understand how engineers actually work (not just what they ship)

  • Surface meaningful insights about productivity, quality, collaboration and impact

  • Help teams improve outcomes without vanity metrics or surveillance

Our goal is not to optimize for “more output,” but for better engineering.

The Team You’ll Work With

You’ll work directly with:

  • Andrew (CTO) – previously a founding engineer at Causal, MIT alum. Andrew has been in your shoes and is deeply committed to providing the mentorship, ownership and growth he had as an early engineer.

  • Adam (CEO) – leads sales and customer discovery. Adam is a former sales executive at multiple high-growth startups and deeply embedded with customers and scaled multiple sales teams from $0-30M in ARR.

This is a small, intense, highly collaborative team. You will have real ownership from day one.

Responsibilities

  • Own the customer relationship post-sale. From onboarding, to account management, to technical support.

  • Partner closely with founders, engineers, and product to influence roadmap & strategy.

  • Act as the first responder to incoming support tickets, triaging and resolving issues efficiently.

  • Diagnose and troubleshoot technical problems across GCP and our own systems.

  • Reproduce issues and create clear, actionable bug reports for engineering.

  • Submit small pull requests for simple fixes, documentation updates, or configuration changes.

  • Collaborate with product and engineering teams to resolve escalations quickly.

  • Keep support documentation up to date.

Requirements

  • Engineering background (software, DevOps, or similar) with strong technical problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to read and write code; confident making simple PRs in GitHub or similar.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Desire to talk to customers and ability to handle intense situations.

  • Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment.

  • This role is 5 days in office in SF

Nice to Have

  • Experience with developer tools or SaaS products.

  • Previous experience in a technical support or solutions engineering role.

Why Join

  • Competitive pay + early equity

  • Health/vision/dental insurance covered

  • Free lunch/dinners/snacks

  • Yearly team offsite with regular team events

  • Yearly $500 learning/development stipend

  • Get to work in SF with one of the fastest moving teams (95%+ percentile code output)

About the interview

  1. 15-minute intro call

  2. Take home assessment

  3. 30 min culture interview with CEO

  4. 30 min interview with Founders

  5. 50 min interview with CEO
